title: Monetary Policy and Economic Developments - Federal Reserve
summary: The February 2019 Monetary Policy Report reviews U.S. economic developments in 2018, during which the FOMC raised the federal funds rate target range twice to reach 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, then signaled a patient approach at the January 2019 meeting amid softer global conditions and muted inflation. The labor market remained strong with payrolls averaging 224,000/month since June, while PCE inflation fell to an estimated 1.7% in December from slightly above the 2% objective earlier in the year.
key_points: FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate twice in H2 2018, reaching 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent after the December meeting
The January 2019 FOMC statement indicated the Committee will be patient in determining future rate adjustments, citing softer global economic and financial conditions late in 2018
Payroll employment growth averaged 224,000 per month since June 2018; unemployment rate held near 4 percent, a low level by historical standards
PCE inflation declined to an estimated 1.7 percent in December 2018 from slightly above the 2 percent objective in mid-year, with core inflation at 1.9 percent
Real GDP increased at a solid rate in H2 2018 and rose slightly under 3 percent for the full year, a pickup from recent years
Financial conditions became less supportive of growth since July 2018; risk appetite deteriorated markedly in Q4 amid concerns about global growth outlook and trade tensions
Foreign economic growth slowed significantly in 2018, particularly in the euro area and China; advanced foreign economy central banks maintained accommodative policies
why_it_matters: This Federal Reserve report documents the 2018 monetary policy trajectory and the shift to a patient stance in early 2019. Understanding this policy pivot—raising rates to 2.25-2.50% then signaling a pause—provides historical context for how the Fed responds to emerging downside risks and soft inflation. For macro trading, this illustrates the FOMC's reaction function when inflation falls below target amid global growth concerns.
macro_context: The report documents the Fed's H2 2018 tightening cycle (four total 2018 hikes) followed by a pronounced dovish pivot signaled in January 2019. This pause came as PCE inflation fell below the 2% objective, global growth slowed (especially euro area and China), and financial conditions tightened amid trade tensions and risk-off episodes. The labor market remained robust but inflation pressures receded, prompting the patient stance.
